final_codebook.domain: Subtracting fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Align fractional forms
skills.definition: Rewrite quantities so their fractional parts are compatible for subtraction by finding or recognizing a common denominator, including rewriting a whole number with a zero fractional part when that serves denominator alignment.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step finds an LCD/common denominator and converts one or both fractions to equivalent fractions.
Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0/n so its fractional part matches the denominator used in the subtraction setup.
Tag when mixed-number fraction parts are explicitly rewritten to share a denominator before subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators already match and no alignment or equivalent-fraction rewriting is performed.
Do not tag converting an improper mixed number such as 2 3/2 to 3 1/2; that is S02.
Do not tag the actual subtraction, borrowing, or simplification steps.

skills.name: Normalize mixed numbers
skills.definition: Convert a mixed number with an improper fractional part into an equivalent standard mixed number before subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a mixed number like 2 3/2 or 1 5/3 is rewritten as an equivalent mixed number with a proper fractional part.
Tag when the solver explicitly normalizes the whole and fractional parts of an improper mixed number before subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag ordinary common-denominator work or equivalent-fraction conversion; that is S01.
Do not tag rewriting a whole number as a whole plus 0/n; that is S01 rather than normalization.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping during subtraction; that is S04.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Carry out the subtraction once forms are compatible, including subtracting numerators of like-denominator fractions and subtracting whole and fractional parts when no regrouping is the focus.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when like-denominator fractions are subtracted by subtracting numerators.
Tag when whole parts and fraction parts of mixed numbers are subtracted directly without borrowing.
Tag when the solver combines the resulting whole and fractional parts into the answer, provided no borrowing or simplification is the main operation of the step.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag denominator-finding, equivalent-fraction rewriting, or rewriting a whole as 0/n; those are S01.
Do not tag normalization of improper mixed numbers; that is S02.
Do not tag steps whose key operation is borrowing/regrouping or reduction to lowest terms; those are S04.

skills.name: Regroup or simplify
skills.definition: Regroup one whole as fractional units when needed to complete subtraction, and/or simplify the resulting fraction or mixed number to lowest terms or integer form.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step borrows 1 from the whole part and converts it into n/n fractional units to continue subtraction.
Tag when the solver resolves a negative fractional difference by regrouping across whole and fractional parts.
Tag when a result is reduced to lowest terms, a zero fraction is simplified to an integer, or the final answer is expressed in simplified form after subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag straightforward subtraction that requires no regrouping and no simplification beyond the raw difference; that is S03.
Do not tag common-denominator conversion or rewriting a whole as 0/n before subtraction; that is S01.
Do not tag normalization of improper mixed numbers; that is S02.

decisions.reasoning: C01 had 3/3 consensus and is independently testable from subtraction and borrowing. It covers common-denominator work and the aligned use of 0/n rewrites without becoming overly broad.

C02 had 3/3 consensus and is distinct from denominator alignment: normalizing an improper mixed number can occur even when no denominator change is needed. Keeping it improves diagnostic resolution for items such as FS04, FS11, FS19, and FS20.

decisions.details: Removed C03 as a standalone skill
decisions.reasoning: C03 had only 1/3 consensus and lacked stable independence. Its whole-number-as-0/n cases are better absorbed into S01, while its broader decomposition cases are either ordinary setup embedded in subtraction or too inconsistently defined for reliable annotation.
C04 had 3/3 consensus and represents the core subtraction operation after preparation is complete. It is clearly distinct from alignment, normalization, and regrouping.

The final codebook must contain exactly 4 skills, and simplification alone would be too sparse and not independently robust across the item set. Borrowing and simplification frequently occur in the same end-stage resolution process, and combining them preserves coverage while maintaining a usable, clearly bounded skill.

decisions.details: Refined S04 to include both regrouping and final simplification, while excluding ordinary subtraction and initial rewriting
decisions.reasoning: This refinement resolves the A/B versus C granularity difference and ensures complete coverage of steps like FS08 Step2 and FS05 Step5-6 without creating a fifth skill.

summary: The consolidation retained the four most diagnostically useful operations: aligning fractional forms, normalizing improper mixed numbers, subtracting aligned parts, and a combined regroup/simplify skill. A low-consensus rewrite skill was removed because its content was better absorbed into alignment or subtraction. Borrowing and simplification were merged to satisfy the four-skill constraint while preserving complete coverage and clear annotation boundaries.
